query: Index every markdown file in ./docs into a TopK collection named `<collection>` so I can search them. Then run a hybrid search (semantic similarity plus BM25 keyword score) for each of these queries and show me the real top 5 files with their scores, one result per file: "how do I filter by metadata", "read your own writes consistency", "maximum document size".
expected_behavior: Uses the topk CLI (`topk import`, `topk sql`), not a hand-written loader or SDK program
Chunks long files so all text is searchable; no `TextTooLong` failure on collections-query.md (48k characters) and no truncation
Passes `-f` with a semantic index on the chunk text and checks the plan with `--dry-run` before importing
Uses `should()` or `match()` in WHERE whenever bm25_score() is selected, and applies hybrid weights in ORDER BY
Returns one result per file by keeping each file's best chunk (not by storing one document per file)
Confirms the count matches the number of chunks written
"maximum document size" ranks limits.md first

query: Load products.json into a TopK collection named `<collection>`. Then find the 5 most relevant in-stock products for each search below. Rank mainly by how semantically relevant the product's name and description are to the query, but boost products whose name contains words from the query. Show me the real results for: "something to block noise while I work"; "coffee" under $100; "shoes for running" in the outdoor category.
expected_behavior: Uses `topk import` with `-f` (semantic indexes on name and description), not a loader script
Uses one index per field
Filters on in_stock, plus category and max price when given, inside the query (WHERE), with price compared as a float or in cents
Boosts name matches with boost(…, match_any(name, …), …) in ORDER BY
"something to block noise while I work" ranks the Noise Machine for Focus first

query: I run a support bot for several customers. Each customer's docs are in ./tenants/<customer>/*.md. Index them into a TopK collection named `<collection>`, keeping each customer's data isolated so one customer can never see another's. Some files are long; all of their text must be searchable. Then show me real search results for: 1. acme: "what is the max document size" 2. "how do I delete documents" for both acme and globex, showing acme cannot see globex's content 3. delete all of globex's data, then show that searching globex returns nothing.
expected_behavior: Uses one partition per customer (`--partition`, `collection$customer` or `collection PARTITION customer`), not a tenant filter
Chunks long files so all text is indexed (no truncation)
Never returns globex content for acme searches
Deletes globex with `DELETE FROM <collection>$globex` and re-checks reads until they fail with `Partition does not exist` before reporting success, rather than assuming a fixed wait was enough
Treats `Partition does not exist` as no results

query: Load ./articles.jsonl into a TopK collection named `<collection>` so I can search the articles by meaning. I don't want to write any code for this. Then show me the real top 5 results for: "how do I filter by metadata", "maximum document size", "read your own writes consistency".
expected_behavior: Uses the topk CLI (`topk import`, `topk sql`), not a hand-written loader
Runs `topk import --dry-run` with `-f` naming the indexed fields before importing, because without `-f` nothing is indexed
Handles the article over 32,768 characters (collections/query) without losing text: checks text lengths and chunks first or uses a keyword index, rather than letting import cut it off silently
Passes `--yes` to the import and never runs an interactive command
Confirms with `SELECT COUNT(*)` that the collection holds as many documents as were written
Runs semantic searches with `topk sql` and shows the real output; "maximum document size" ranks limits first
